title: Annealing schedule and max-cut quality
question: Per annealing run (50 per schedule, 1 to 500 sweeps): does the cut as a share of the best (ratio) rise with the sweeps?

issues.text: One graph, one temperature range (2 to 0.05) and seeded runs: the trend holds for this setup, not for annealing in general.
issues.fix: Change GRAPH in the Graph step and rerun; the hard cases are random graphs with many odd cycles.

issues.text: Time per run grows with sweeps, so 'better' here is bought with more work.
issues.fix: Read the success curve per unit of work: found_best_pct against sweeps × n moves.

issues.text: Simulated annealing stands in for D-Wave's quantum annealer only by analogy: the QPU uses quantum fluctuations, a fixed anneal time, and noise.
issues.fix: Compare with the QPU on the same graph (the D-Wave board) before concluding about quantum annealing.

alternatives.question: Is the share of runs that find the exact best (hit) higher with longer schedules?
alternatives.why: Drills from the mean ratio to the yes/no outcome a user cares about.

alternatives.question: On the random 22-node graph, does annealing need more sweeps than on the 3-regular one to reach 90% success?
alternatives.why: Expands to how the graph's structure makes the landscape harder.

alternatives.question: Does D-Wave's QPU find the best cut more often with a longer anneal time (1 to 2,000 µs)?
alternatives.why: Expands to the quantum annealer itself; needs a Leap token and the D-Wave board.

hypotheses.statement: The cut found, as a share of the best cut, rises with the annealing schedule (sweeps).
hypotheses.null: The cut found does not depend on the schedule length.

concepts.label: Split
concepts.description: An assignment of every node to side A or side B.

concepts.label: Cut quality
concepts.description: Links cut by the run's final split, divided by the maximum cut found by exhaustive search.

concepts.label: Annealing schedule
concepts.description: Sweeps: the schedule has sweeps × n moves while the temperature falls from 2 to 0.05.
concepts.why: The predictor; 0 is a random split.

concepts.label: Found the best
concepts.description: 1 when the run's cut equals the maximum cut.
concepts.why: The yes/no version of the outcome.

data.request: For the same graph: D-Wave QPU samples (num_reads 100) at anneal times 1, 20, 200 and 2,000 µs
data.source: D-Wave Leap Solver API, with your own token
data.why: To put the quantum annealer on the same curve.

method.summary: Spearman's rank correlation between sweeps and the cut ratio over all 500 runs; a positive ρ with an interval above 0 supports H1. The summary table gives the success rate per schedule.

steps.title: The graph
steps.detail: Links of the chosen graph (Graph step); the exact landscape and best cut by Gray-code search (Every split, Best split).

steps.title: Anneal
steps.detail: 50 seeded runs per schedule from 1 to 500 sweeps, plus 50 random splits (Annealing runs).

steps.title: Cut quality
steps.detail: ratio = cut / max cut and hit = 1 at the best, per run.

steps.title: Rises or not
steps.detail: Spearman ρ of ratio on sweeps; read the success curve for where it levels off.

caveats: Seeded runs: the numbers are reproducible but are one sample of 50 per schedule.
The exhaustive search is exact only up to about 26 nodes in a browser; beyond that the 'best' would be a guess.
Simulated annealing is an analogy for the quantum annealer, not a model of it.
